name: THE BAR
note:
A section of the bar, its stools and the man at it -- one object, drawn together.
FITTED, AND MEASURED BEFORE WIRING: the whole bar came back at x1126-1916 y356-849 against the x1126-1916 y355-849 it replaces -- 1.00x, every edge to the pixel. The previous attempt was 1.55x and 432 pixels too far into the room, and was shipped because the comparison was never run. Giving the generator the footprint as a red box on the original was what fixed it: a box to fit rather than a description to interpret.
Three sections because the bar runs 490 pixels in depth and one anchor cannot put Thad in front of the near end and behind the far one. Cut at x1290 and x1500, where the sprite is bar only; recomposed against the whole, maximum channel difference ZERO. The far end: the man seated on his stool, back to the room.

sprite.note:
A FOUR-FRAME BREATH, DERIVED FROM THE ONE DRAWING. A second generation was tried and measured: asked for this furniture with nobody at it, the generator hit the bounding box exactly and then repeated only 26% of the furniture pixels within twelve levels -- mean difference 29.2 where it should have been zero. Frames built from two such drawings would make the furniture shimmer under men who are meant to be still.
So each man’s own columns lift one pixel and every other pixel is copied verbatim: ZERO pixels ever change outside the declared columns, so the furniture cannot move. Each man is up for two frames of four, offset one frame from his neighbour, so no two breathe in step -- ruling 20’s point about synchronised idles, indoors.
